name: pinned-paid-judge-default
question: Production is switching its default judge from the free OpenAI-style chain (measured provider reliability 0.295-0.808 on 312-call packs) to ONE pinned paid model (anthropic claude-sonnet-5). Does the pinned paid model clear the reliability floor and raise reliability without regressing verdict quality against the incumbent chain?
hypothesis: the same shipped v5 prompt on one pinned paid model (anthropic claude-sonnet-5) raises provider reliability by >= 0.05 versus the incumbent free chain without regressing fixture agreement, ECE, fake-citation influence or any invariance stability metric beyond their registered caps
singleVariable: JUDGE PROVIDER/MODEL ONLY: baseline = incumbent free chain (unorouter nemotron-3.5-lightning:free); candidate = single pinned paid model (anthropic claude-sonnet-5). Byte-identical v5 system prompt (default citation clause), identical fixtures, temperature 0, tie threshold, retry policy and scoring; nothing else differs.
providerNote: study-level models (unorouter) keeps the capacity plan and baseline probe on the incumbent chain; each arm carries its own models so the candidate arm probes and runs anthropic. Requires UNOROUTER_API_KEY AND ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
executionStatus: READY - both arms implemented (anthropic judge selectable via --models anthropic; per-arm models probed before every arm). Declare a call budget: expected 2340 calls, so pass --budget-calls 3000 (or set JUDGE_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET).
adoptionRule: supported iff usable runs >= 3/arm at reliability >= 0.75 AND target "provider reliability" moves up by >= 0.05 AND the bootstrap 90% CI lower bound of the signed improvement is > 0 AND no protected metric regresses beyond its cap AND pooled run sd. Fewer usable runs, any unmet condition or missing data => INCONCLUSIVE. Gate thresholds are untouchable.
